sections.h2: What should a seller know about Ross Township, PA?
sections.html:
Ross Township is a large suburb on the northern edge of Pittsburgh in Allegheny County, with a retail-heavy McKnight Road corridor, an older population and a transfer tax that is split between the township and the North Hills School District. A sale here is handled through the Allegheny County Division of Real Estate and the township's Building office.

The township was incorporated on June 26, 1809 and was named for James Ross, a Pittsburgh attorney and U.S. Senator. It covers 14.47 square miles, surrounds West View Borough, and shares eleven borders with municipalities including McCandless, Hampton, Shaler, Franklin Park and the Pittsburgh neighborhoods of Perry North and Brighton Heights. Northway Mall opened in 1962 as the first enclosed mall in Pennsylvania, and the Big Mac was created in 1967 at a McDonald's on McKnight Road.

The notes below cover what buyers see, what the township and county require, and how a fast sale compares with a listing.

sections.h2: What do Census figures show about Ross homes and owners?
sections.html:
Ross has a mature, mostly owner-occupied housing market, with a high share of older residents and a population estimate that has slipped since 2020.

With nearly a quarter of residents 65 or older and an average of 2.22 people per household, a share of Ross houses are held by older owners, and a sale of a long-held home often needs a repair estimate before pricing.

sections.h2: Do I need an occupancy certificate to sell a house in Ross Township?
sections.html:
Ask the Building office before you list. The township's Building page says that department handles permit applications, plan review, inspections and Certificates of Occupancy under the Pennsylvania Uniform Construction Code, but it does not describe a separate resale inspection.

Call the Building Inspections office at 412-931-7048, open Monday through Friday from 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. at 1000 Ross Municipal Drive, and ask whether your address needs anything for a transfer. If you did work on the house without a permit, resolve it before a buyer's inspector finds it.

  • Permits are applied for online through iWorq.
  • Inspections need 48 hours' notice, and requests must include the permit number, address, inspection type, preferred date and an on-site contact.
  • Plumbing permits and inspections run through the Allegheny County Health Department, and electrical inspections go through the township's third-party agency.
  • For flood questions, the township says it cannot certify flood zones. Properties in a FEMA Special Flood Hazard Area face added requirements, so check the FEMA map for your parcel.

Projects submitted after January 1, 2026 follow the 2021 International codes as amended by the state, so a buyer's renovation plans will be reviewed under the newer codes.

sections.h2: How much transfer tax do sellers in Ross pay?
sections.html:
Allegheny County says its realty transfer tax runs from 2% to 5% of the price, with 1% going to the state and the rest split between the municipality and the school district. For Ross, ask the Division of Real Estate for the exact municipal and North Hills School District rates, which the county posts on its local rate page.

The county provides two examples. In Shaler Township, a $40,000 house carries 1% state, 0.5% township and 0.5% school tax for a 2% total of $800. In the City of Pittsburgh, the same house carries a total of 5%, which is $2,000. Use those as a guide to the arithmetic only, because Ross has its own rates.

  • The county collects state and local transfer tax when the deed is recorded, paid on a separate check from the recording fees.
  • A Statement of Value (REV-183) is required when the deed does not list the consideration or when an exemption applies.
  • Certain transfers between family members may be exempt, and the deed should say so, for example by stating that the transfer is familial and exempt from realty transfer tax.
  • The Department of Revenue can answer exemption questions at 717-783-8104.

At the Census median value of $268,900, each 1% of tax is about $2,690, so a 2% total would be near $5,400 and a 3% total near $8,100.

sections.h2: How do assessments and appeals work for Ross homeowners?
sections.html:
Allegheny County assesses Ross properties, and the first level of appeal is the Board of Property Assessment Appeals and Review. Owners and any taxing body with an interest in the parcel can file. Hearings are held by telephone, and a lawyer is optional, although most school districts and municipalities bring counsel.

If the BPAAR result is unsatisfactory, either side can take the appeal to the second level, the Board of Viewers at the Court of Common Pleas. Only the filing party can withdraw an appeal, using the county's withdrawal form. The county also allows year-round special appeals when the Office of Property Assessments issues a written determination in certain circumstances.

The school district and the township can appeal an assessment too. If you receive a hearing notice for an appeal filed by the school district or the municipality on your home, you may attend but you are not required to. A buyer who learns of a pending taxing-body appeal will ask about it, so mention it during negotiations.

sections.h2: Which neighborhoods, schools and roads matter in Ross?
sections.html:
Ross and West View together form the North Hills School District, which also uses Northland Public Library, shared among several municipalities. North Hills High School is the district's high school, and the school district is a recurring point in listings.

The township's named areas include Perrysville, McKnight, Evergreen Hamlet, Berkeley Hills, Highcliff, Laurel Gardens, North Hills Estates, Kinvara, Greybrooke, Holly Hill, White Oak Heights, Glenshaw, Keown Station and Northway. Commercial districts cluster along McKnight Road, U.S. Route 19 (Perry Highway) and Babcock Boulevard.

The township's population rose from about 15,700 in 1950 to about 35,100 in 1980, so homes in Evergreen Hamlet, Perrysville and the newer plans differ widely in age. Describe your street, lot and era in your listing or offer request, because buyers search by those features.

sections.h2: Should I list or take a cash offer in Ross?
sections.html:
List when the house shows well and you can wait for lender timelines. Take a cash offer when the house needs work, an estate is involved or the date matters more than the last few thousand dollars.

  • Compare offers by net proceeds after transfer tax, any commission, repairs and unpaid taxes.
  • Ask each buyer in writing who pays transfer tax and what happens if an inspection finds a defect.
  • Confirm the closing date and whether the buyer can close without a mortgage contingency.

faqs.q: Who issues Certificates of Occupancy in Ross Township?
faqs.a: The township Building department. It handles permits, plan review, inspections and Certificates of Occupancy under the Pennsylvania Uniform Construction Code, and its inspections line is 412-931-7048.

faqs.q: What is the transfer tax range in Allegheny County?
faqs.a: Allegheny County reports a range of 2% to 5% of the price, with 1% to the state and the remainder to the municipality and school district. Ask the county for the specific Ross and North Hills School District rates.

faqs.q: Can I appeal my Ross assessment before selling?
faqs.a: Yes. The owner or any taxing body can file with the Board of Property Assessment Appeals and Review. A lawyer is not required, and the county lists the appeal forms and a withdrawal form on its Appeals page.

faqs.q: Is a house in a FEMA flood zone harder to sell in Ross?
faqs.a: It can be, because properties in a Special Flood Hazard Area face added requirements. The township cannot certify flood zones, so check the FEMA map for your parcel and tell buyers early.

faqs.q: Which school district serves Ross Township?
faqs.a: The North Hills School District, which also serves West View Borough. North Hills High School is the district's high school.
